controls.label: OddWire Forms
controls.value: OddWire.Form turns reusable form definitions into working documents. Each form describes what information can be shown or entered, how that information is organised, and which optional tools the form supports.

controls.label: Forms and documents
controls.value: A form is the reusable template. A document is one filled copy of that form. You can create multiple documents from the same form without changing the original template.

controls.label: How to navigate
controls.value: Use the tabs along the bottom to move between major sections. Some forms also contain smaller tab groups, expandable panels, repeating lists, and pop-up sections.

controls.label: This guide
controls.value: This About Forms document is read-only. It demonstrates the same tab and presentation system used by working forms, but it does not collect or export information.

controls.label: What OddWire.Form is for
controls.value: OddWire.Form is a configurable data-capture and document application. Forms define the fields, layout, presentation, and optional integrations; documents hold the information entered against those definitions.

controls.label: Start a document
controls.value: Open a form from the Forms list, then create or open one of its documents. The form supplies the available fields and defaults; the document stores your changes.

controls.label: Enter information
controls.value: Text fields accept short values. Larger text areas accept notes or paragraphs. Checkboxes store yes-or-no choices. Dropdowns and radio groups select from the options supplied by the form.

controls.label: Lookup fields
controls.value: Some dropdowns load choices from a lookup table. Selecting a record may fill other matching fields automatically. Review the filled values before relying on them.

controls.label: Repeating sections
controls.value: A repeating section can hold several rows of the same structure, such as tasks, traits, attacks, contacts, or inventory items. Use Add Row when the form allows additional entries.

controls.label: Document lists
controls.value: A form may use selected fields to name, group, filter, or order its documents. Changing those fields can also change how the document appears in the list.

controls.label: Read-only forms
controls.value: Some forms are presentations or reference documents rather than data-entry forms. These may contain only labels, images, and navigation controls.

controls.label: Automatic values
controls.value: Calculated or lookup-filled values may update when their source fields change. Review automatic values before relying on them.

controls.label: Form capabilities
controls.value: Each form defines its own controls, lookup data, layout, and optional export actions. Features available in one form may not exist in another.

controls.label: Fields
controls.value: Forms may contain text, long text, checkbox, image, dropdown, radio, and calculated display fields. A disabled field can be read but not edited. A hidden field is not shown in the form.

controls.label: Tabs
controls.value: Tabs divide a large form into focused pages. The bottom navigation is the form's main tab set. Tabs inside a page create a smaller local tab set.

controls.label: Expandable panels
controls.value: Expandable panels keep detailed sections compact. Select the panel heading to reveal or hide its contents. The heading may include values from fields inside the panel.

controls.label: Pop-ups
controls.value: A pop-up opens a temporary focused view over the current page. Closing it returns you to the same place in the form.

controls.label: Responsive layout
controls.value: Forms rearrange their columns to suit the available screen width. Fields that appear side by side on a wide screen may stack vertically on a phone.

controls.label: Labels and calculated information
controls.value: Some displayed values are explanatory text or are assembled from other fields. They may not be editable even when they update alongside the document.

controls.label: Local storage
controls.value: OddWire.Form is memory-first and persists documents locally in the current application or browser environment. Form definitions and document values remain separate.

controls.label: Saving changes
controls.value: Edits update the current document as field values change. A document stores only its own values and overrides; unchanged fields continue to use the form definition.

controls.label: Backups and removal
controls.value: Clearing application or browser data may remove locally stored documents unless they have been backed up or exported through another supported mechanism.

controls.label: Local does not mean encrypted
controls.value: Local storage should not be assumed to be encrypted, access-controlled, or suitable for regulated information. Security depends on the device, browser, deployment, and surrounding environment.

controls.label: Review your data
controls.value: A form controls presentation and data shape, not factual accuracy. Imported, lookup-filled, calculated, or manually entered values should be checked before use.

controls.label: Optional exports
controls.value: Some forms may provide export actions when their author has configured them. Export behaviour belongs to that form. This About Forms guide has no export configuration.

controls.label: Sensitive information
controls.value: Do not enter confidential, regulated, or personally sensitive information unless you understand how your copy of the application stores, backs up, shares, and removes local data.
